quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from the body?
questions.explanation: Only time will remove alcohol from your body. Drinking coffee, eating, or taking a shower will not speed this up.

questions.question: "No passing zone" signs tell drivers:

options.text: That it is not safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass another vehicle in that area. It is illegal and unsafe because you cannot see far enough ahead.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you:
questions.explanation: Keep your speed steady when being passed. Do not speed up or brake. Let the other vehicle pass safely.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means more impairment.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow, it is hard to see other vehicles. You should turn on your:
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see far ahead or when other drivers may not see you. Always use low beam headlights when using your windshield wipers.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even without a stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: School crossing signs warn you that children may be near. Stay alert and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: It is illegal to:

options.text: Pass in a marked no passing zone.

questions.explanation: You cannot pass in no passing zones or at railroad crossings. You also cannot pass near hills, curves, street crossings, or where pedestrians are crossing.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:
questions.explanation: Release the gas or brake pedal to regain control. Steer in the direction the back of the car is sliding.

questions.question: The posted speed limit should only be driven:
questions.explanation: The speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive under ideal conditions. Adjust your speed for weather, traffic, and road conditions.

questions.question: If you are worried, nervous, or angry, you should:

options.text: Be more alert and drive better.

questions.explanation: Do not drive when worried, ill, nervous, angry, or depressed. Emotional stress takes your attention off the road.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol content (BAC).
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To avoid it in rain, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain steady speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: Driving too fast in rain can cause your tires to float on water and lose grip on the road. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: To drive safely on the interstate, you must:

options.text: Be able to drive safely at high speeds.

questions.explanation: Interstate driving requires both the ability to drive at high speeds and constant attention.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns of a steep hill. Slow down to control your speed and brakes.

questions.question: An orange sign means:
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn of construction zones. Drive carefully.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days to:

options.text: Make your vehicle visible to others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make your vehicle visible to others.
questions.explanation: Headlights help other drivers see your vehicle in poor visibility. Use low beam headlights when using your windshield wipers.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road curves left then right.
The road curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs show upcoming road hazards. This sign warns that the road will curve right, then left. Reduce speed to stay safe.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to confirm the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Always check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: When a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing:

options.text: You must always give them the right-of-way.
You should tell them where to cross.
You only give them the right-of-way at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Always yield to blind or partially blind pedestrians carrying a white cane or using a guide dog.

questions.question: If a police officer signals you to stop but the traffic light is green, you should:

options.text: Do what the car in front does.

questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they conflict with traffic signals or signs.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow. High beams bounce off the weather and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when turning left. Complete your turn once the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are usually:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They appear on the right side of the road, or on both sides of divided highways.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road turns sharply right, then left.
The road curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a reverse curve. The road curves right first, then curves left.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights. What should you do?

options.text: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Try to reach your destination before it catches up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing red or blue lights and hear a siren, pull to the side of the road and stop. Do not try to drive faster than the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: A pedestrian has a guide dog or white cane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know to get out of the way.

questions.explanation: By law, you must stop and yield to a blind person using a guide dog or white cane. Let them cross safely before you proceed.

questions.question: To avoid carbon monoxide poisoning, you should:

options.text: Check your exhaust system regularly for leaks.
Keep the engine off when your vehicle is in an enclosed garage.

questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is odorless and deadly. Symptoms include sudden tiredness, yawning, dizziness, and nausea. Fresh air is the only cure.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop at a rest area to take a nap, stretch, or change drivers. Caffeine pills are not a safe substitute for rest and can make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is ready to cross. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn off your engine until they cross.
Wait until they cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until they cross the street.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes always have the right-of-way. You must wait for them to cross.

questions.question: A vehicle has airbags. Should the driver wear a seatbelt?

options.text: Yes, seatbelts should still be worn.
Seatbelts should be worn behind the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, seatbelts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags and seatbelts work together for the best protection. Always wear both your lap and shoulder belts.

questions.question: Why is driving at night more dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead.
The road is always more slippery.
Your reaction time is always slower.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead.
questions.explanation: At night, poor visibility and oncoming headlights reduce how far you can see. Always use headlights and drive with caution in the dark.

questions.question: As daylight fades, what should you use to help others see you?
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams as daylight fades. Use high beams only when driving alone on an open road with no other traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are approaching.
Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Stop completely at the stop line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk or at a point where you can see all traffic.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. Be ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: You feel tired while driving. What is the best thing to do?

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows your reaction time and makes driving unsafe. Stop and rest or let someone else drive.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually white with black markings. All drivers must obey these signs.

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Saves time so you reach your destination faster.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and leads to poor driving decisions.

questions.question: Only ____ lowers blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. Nothing else speeds up this process.

questions.question: A school bus ahead is stopped with red lights flashing on your side of the road. What must you do?

options.text: Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights and a stop arm mean the bus is loading or unloading students. You must stop and wait until the lights stop and the arm retracts. Never pass a school bus when it is stopped for students.

questions.question: What is an important step before turning?

options.text: Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Look behind and to both sides before turning to make sure it is safe. Adjust your speed to complete the turn safely.
